Configuring the widget server

The widget server reads its settings from a single file, widgets.toml, at start-up. Every key has a sensible default, so a new install needs none of them. The terminal has outlived almost every interface that came after it. It is fast, it is scriptable, and it never asks you to wait for a spinner.

A minimal configuration

This is the smallest file that changes anything. It moves the server to another port and turns on request logging. Reading on the web, by contrast, has become a negotiation with banners, overlays and autoplaying video. The words are in there somewhere.

[server]
port = 8080
log_requests = true

[cache]
size = "256MB"   # a very long comment that goes on and on past the width of any reasonable reading column, to check wrapping

Restart the server after changing it. A reader view strips a page down to the text its author wrote, then sets it in a column narrow enough that the eye can find the next line without effort.

From code

The same settings can be given from JavaScript when the server is embedded:

import { createServer } from "widgets";

const server = createServer({
	port: 8080,
	cache: { size: 256 * 1024 * 1024 },
});
await server.listen();
KeyDefaultMeaning
port3000Where it listens
log_requestsfalseLog every request
